c.tagline: Antigua's cruise-port capital of Georgian quays, 365 beaches, and Nelson's Dockyard sailing.

taxi.fareNote: Taxis are unmetered with government-set fixed rates by zone — always agree the fare before departing. There is no Uber. US dollars are widely accepted alongside EC dollars, usually at a 2.7 rate.

emergency.note: 911 and 999 both reach police, fire and ambulance; the main hospital is the Sir Lester Bird Medical Centre in St. John's.

english.label: Easy to get by in English

avoid.reason: Petty theft occurs around the cruise quays, market and beaches — don't leave valuables unattended, and avoid unlit back streets after dark.

hood_desc: The commercial and cruise heart of the capital, where ships dock at Heritage Quay's duty-free malls, jewellers and boutiques beneath the twin white towers of St. John's Cathedral.
The near-north coast around historic Fort James guarding the harbour mouth, with calm town beaches at Fort James and Runaway Bay a short ride from downtown.
The island's most popular resort strip just north of the city — a long white-sand bay lined with hotels, beach bars, watersports and sunset catamarans.
A quieter upscale north-coast stretch of resorts, villas and small beaches beyond the airport turn, good for a calm base near town and reef snorkeling.
lodging: Ocean Point Beach Resort & Spa Adults Only

water.note: The desalinated supply is officially potable but inconsistent; most visitors drink bottled.

transit.pay: Public minibuses (vans) charge a low flat cash fare in EC dollars and leave from the West Bus Station (for the west and north) and East Bus Station (for the south and English Harbour). Taxis are unmetered with government-set zone fares.
transit.hours: Minibuses run frequently in daylight, thin out by early evening and rarely run on Sundays; taxis are the reliable option after dark.
transit.note: There is no rail or organized city bus service — shared minibuses and taxis are the only public transport. US dollars are widely accepted alongside EC dollars.

bus: Antigua public minibus network (West and East Bus Stations)

car.idp: Required (a local temporary driving permit must be purchased)

ferry: Cruise ships dock at Heritage Quay and the Deep Water Harbour

transit.m: Taxi to St. John's (fixed fare, 15-20 min)
Public minibus from the nearby main road (daytime only)

tip.r: A 10% service charge is often added to hotel and restaurant bills; if not, 10-15% is customary, and tip taxi drivers around 10%.

landmarks: St. John's Cathedral (Cathedral of St John the Divine)
The twin baroque towers of this 1840s Anglican cathedral dominate the skyline, its earthquake-resistant pitch-pine interior a marvel of Caribbean craftsmanship.
Redcliffe Quay
A waterfront quarter of restored colonial warehouses and slave-trade-era buildings, now Antigua's most atmospheric enclave of boutiques, cafes and galleries.
Heritage Quay
The cruise-ship gateway's duty-free shopping complex, where pastel arcades, vendors' stalls and harbour views buzz whenever liners are in port.
Museum of Antigua and Barbuda
Housed in the 1750 colonial courthouse, St John's oldest building, tracing island history from Arawak settlement to independence, with Viv Richards' cricket bat.
Fort James
An 18th-century harbour-mouth fort still bristling with original cannon, guarding golden Fort James Beach and sunset views over St John's Harbour.
Public Market (Heritage Market)
St John's bustling Saturday-morning institution, piled with black pineapples, mangoes, spices and crafts amid nonstop Antiguan banter.
Fort Barrington
A 1779 hilltop fort at Deep Bay reached by a short scramble, rewarding hikers with 360-degree views over Five Islands and the capital.
Dickenson Bay
Antigua's classic resort beach just north of the capital, a mile of powder-white sand and calm turquoise water lined with bars and watersports.
Antigua Recreation Ground
The island's original Test cricket ground in the heart of St. John's, where Viv Richards once smashed the fastest century in Test history.
Government House
The official residence of Antigua's governor since the 19th century, a colonnaded colonial mansion set amid gardens near the heart of St. John's.

train.note: Antigua's old sugar-estate railways closed long ago and there is no passenger rail today. Arrive by air into V. C. Bird International Airport, the main hub for the eastern Caribbean, or by cruise ship into Saint John's.

bus.note: No international coaches - Antigua is an island. Minibuses run from the West Bus Station in Saint John's to the south and west of the island and from the East Bus Station toward the airport and English Harbour, leaving when full rather than to a timetable and stopping early in the evening. Fares are a couple of dollars, paid on board.

intl.op: Montserrat ferry operators — check current schedules locally

ferry.note: There is no regular ferry to the other independent islands - those connections are by air. The Barbuda Express catamaran from the Saint John's waterfront is the only way to reach Barbuda by sea and runs most days, though it is frequently cancelled in rough conditions and the crossing is notoriously bumpy. The Montserrat service has operated on and off; verify before relying on it.

half.name: Nelson's Dockyard
half.blurb: The world's only continuously working Georgian dockyard, a UNESCO site at English Harbour where Admiral Nelson served, now alive with yachts and heritage inns.

half.name: Shirley Heights Lookout
half.blurb: A restored gun battery 490 feet above English Harbour, famed for Antigua's best panorama and legendary Sunday sunset barbecue parties.
